title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
hints: ladders are strictly better than bricks for expensive climbs since they're free regardless of height difference - you want to save your limited ladders for the biggest climbs you'll ever encounter, but you don't know the future in advance
greedily assume every climb gets a ladder, then walk it back: keep a min-heap of the climb sizes you've currently assigned a ladder to

whenever a new climb needs a ladder assignment, tentatively give it one by pushing onto the heap; if that makes the heap exceed your ladder count, evict the smallest climb from the heap (since it least needs a ladder among your assigned climbs) and pay for it with bricks instead
if paying with bricks makes your brick supply go negative, you can't make that climb at all - the furthest building reached is the one just before that failed climb
commonMistakes: assigning ladders to climbs in the order encountered rather than always keeping the ladder set as the largest climbs seen so far
checking bricks against the wrong climb - it must be the smallest of the currently ladder-assigned climbs that gets evicted to bricks, not the new climb itself
not treating downhill or equal-height steps as free moves that never touch bricks or ladders

content.problemStatement:
You're moving left to right across a row of buildings with given
heights, starting at building 0. You have a fixed supply of bricks and
a fixed number of ladders. To step from one building to the next:

- if the next building is the same height or shorter, you can walk over for free
- if the next building is taller, you must climb the height difference, paying with either bricks (cost equals the exact height difference) or a ladder (climbs any height difference for free, but ladders are limited in supply)

**Return the furthest building index you can reach if you spend your bricks and ladders optimally.**
notes: no bricks and no ladders at all, stuck as soon as any climb is required
every step downhill or flat, reaching the last building for free
enough ladders to cover every climb without using any bricks
single building (already at the furthest point with no moves needed)

sampleTestCases.explanation: you can use the ladder on the climb of 5 (building 1 to 2) and bricks on the climb of 3 (building 3 to 4), using all 5 bricks; the next climb of 5 (building 4 to 5) can't be afforded with 0 bricks and no ladders left, so you stop at building 4

using ladders on the two largest climbs (15 and 16) and bricks on the smaller ones (8 and 2, totaling 10 bricks) gets you to building 7 for free (downhill), but the climb of 16 to building 8 can't be afforded
with no ladders, the only climb (16, from building 1 to 2) is paid entirely in bricks, leaving 1 brick, and building 3 is downhill and free, so you reach the last building
